blocks.content: A Persistent Volume Claim is how a Pod actually requests storage, it is a request that gets matched, or "bound," to an available Persistent Volume meeting its requirements.
1. A Request, Not the Storage Itself
blocks.text: 1. A Request, Not the Storage Itself

blocks.content: It is worth being precise about this distinction: a PVC does not directly represent storage, the PV from the previous topic does that, a PVC represents a Pod's request for storage matching certain criteria.

blocks.alt: A request for storage, distinct from the storage resource itself

blocks.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-app-storage
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi

code.content:

kind: PersistentVolumeClaim

blocks.content: Once created, a PVC gets matched, or bound, to an available PV whose capacity and access mode (covered later in this module) satisfy what the claim asked for, this binding is how the abstract request becomes real, usable storage.

blocks.alt: A request, matched to a real, available piece of storage

blocks.content: 3. Pods Reference the Claim, Never the Volume Directly
blocks.text: 3. Pods Reference the Claim, Never the Volume Directly

blocks.content: This is an important architectural detail: a Pod's spec references a PVC, never a PV directly, this indirection is deliberate, it decouples "what storage does my Pod need" from "exactly which physical storage resource provides it."

blocks.alt: A deliberate layer of indirection, the Pod never touches the PV directly

blocks.content:
volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: my-app-storage

code.content:
volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: my-app-storage

codes.yaml:
volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: my-app-storage

blocks.content: Once bound, a PVC and its matched PV are exclusively linked, one PVC binds to exactly one PV, and that PV is not available to satisfy any other claim while the binding exists.

blocks.alt: An exclusive, one-to-one relationship, once established

blocks.content: A PVC binds to a PV based on a few key criteria matching up: requested size (the PV must have enough capacity), access mode (covered in its own topic), and, if specified, StorageClass (covered next), only a PV satisfying all of these is eligible to bind.

blocks.alt: Size, access mode, and storage class, together deciding what counts as a match

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A PVC is a request for storage, matched and bound to an actual PV meeting its size, access mode, and storage class requirements.
Pods reference the PVC, never the PV directly, this indirection cleanly separates what storage a Pod needs from exactly which resource provides it.
